# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-8 (Extended v87)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 2, approximately late 1825-1826)**: Funeral procession for Mother Crucifixion en route to Vaugirard cemetery; Valjean's escape plan executing. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2 (Current)**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak; body placed in vault beneath grand altar during 11 p.m.–midnight procedures; **Following day (sun declining, afternoon/evening)**: Funeral procession departing toward Vaugirard cemetery on Boulevard du Maine.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); **English harbor towns** (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven): Luvie, Wilwick, Gadrek Prydenridge, Isric, Jotho, Tatho Brackick, wife of Tatho planning trip to Elmhaven, children chasing hoop, gulls quarreling over fish heads, wind from water with salt and tar smell. Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **Gorbeau House** (Rue de la Cosette area, Mouffetard): Decrepit lodging where Valjean and Cosette previously lodged; old woman portress; Javert's surveillance station. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars (squares less than 1.5 inches diagonal) riveted by clenched-fist fastenings; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters reinforced with gingerbread-yellow wooden beams, always closed; behind shutters: nun's voice screened by iron grating and plate with thousand holes; slat opens revealing nun's mouth and chin only, covered with black veil, guimpe, shroud. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Lower hall of church communicates with street, no men enter except doctor of dead; **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient cemetery outside regulations, going to be suppressed, has special Permission from Prefecture for nuns to be taken there at nightfall; faded, falling into disuse, dampness invading, flowers deserting, bourgeois prefer Père-Lachaise; venerable enclosure planted like old-fashioned French garden with straight alleys, box, thuya-trees, holly, ancient tombs beneath aged cypress-trees, very tall grass; tragic and lugubrious in evening. **Boulevard du Maine**: Route of funeral procession. **Rue Chemin-Vert**: Location of deaf fruit-seller, good old friend of Fauchelevent, who has little bed available.

## Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration
[Same as before—order lineage, dress, austerity, vows, operational rules, reparation practice, possessions rule, hourly bells, chanting, men allowed]

**MOTHER CRUCIFIXION'S DEATH AND FUNERAL COMPLETION**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak (Winter Year 2). Retained consciousness to last moment, spoke to community then to angels, gave final commands. Prioress described her death as "precious"—smiled, community felt she was regaining life in God. Sisters laid out body. **VAULT BURIAL EXECUTED** (11 p.m.–midnight, same night): Fauchelevent closed coffin; sisters carried coffin to chapel; office for dead said; community returned to cloister. Fauchelevent came with iron bar; Mother Precentors and Mother Ascension present; vault opened beneath grand altar, coffin lowered, vault closed again—no trace, government has no suspicion. Doctor signed death passport. **FUNERAL PROCESSION** (following day, afternoon/evening): Undertaker company brought empty coffin for appearance; hearse ornamented with skulls, cross-bones, tears; coffin covered with white cloth, large black cross; mourning-coach with priest in surplice and choir boy in red cap; two undertaker's men in gray uniforms trimmed with black walked beside hearse; Fauchelevent limped behind in laborer's garments; procession heading toward Vaugirard cemetery on Boulevard du Maine. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage.

## Prioress and Vocal Mothers (1819-1825 Period)
**Mademoiselle de Blemeur (Mother Innocente)** (Prioress, 1819-1825): Age ~sixty; short, thick; "singing like a cracked pot"; excellent woman; only merry one in convent; learned, erudite, wise; proficient in history; descended from Marguerite de Blemeur, author of _Lives of the Saints of the Order of Saint-Benoît_; re-elected. Upon entering on day of death arrangements, double form of preoccupation imprinted on countenance; rose and exclaimed with loquacity of dam breaking away, speaking extensively about Mother Crucifixion's death and spiritual merit. **Vocal Mothers**: Mother Sainte-Honorine; Mother Sainte-Gertrude (treasurer); Mother-Saint-Ange; Mother Annonciation (sacristan); Mother Saint-Augustin (nurse; only malicious one); Mother Sainte-Mechtilde (directs singing); Mother des Anges; Mother Saint-Joseph; Mother Sainte-Adélaide; Mother Miséricorde; Mother Compassion; Mother Providence; **Mother Présentation** (future prioress 1847); Mother Sainte-Céligne; Mother Sainte-Chantal; **Mother Crucifixion** (deceased, Winter Year 2); **Four Mother Precentors** (present at vault opening); **Mother Ascension** (present at vault opening).

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Escape Plan
**PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: Upon learning nun died and funeral procedures commencing, confronted with immediate danger: body removal and convent doors opening; police swarming streets. Turned pale; thought of descending to "terrible street" made him shudder. Pictured entire police force engaged in swarming quarter, agents on watch, sentinels everywhere. Altered appearance reflects sadness, uneasiness, anxiety, depression; continual tremor so long as Cosette near, needs nothing except her, fears nothing except her. **COSETTE'S STATUS**: Woke in cottage; Valjean instructed her to listen attentively, explained they must go away but shall return and be very happy; warned her not to speak and obey, or Madame Thénardier will get her again. **VALJEAN'S TALENTS**: Man who has been prisoner understands how to contract himself to fit diameter of escape. Escape is cure. Possesses gloomy talent: to have himself nailed up in case and carried off like bale of goods, live long time in box, find air where none exists, economize breath for hours, stifle without dying. Demonstrated composure and coolness in crisis—powerful tranquility contagious to others. **CURRENT STATUS**: Executing planned escape via coffin method with Fauchelevent's assistance.

## Fauchelevent's Crucial Role and Escape Plans
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour to traverse short distances; complains of aching back as usual. **PLAN FOR COSETTE**: Will use service door opening on courtyard; knock, porter opens; Cosette placed in vintage basket on his back, covered—"Father Fauchelevent goes out with his basket—perfectly natural"; leave her with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert (good old friend) who has little bed; will shout in fruit-seller's ear that child is his niece, to keep her until tomorrow; Cosette will re-enter with Valjean next day when arranged. **PLAN FOR VALJEAN**: Will hide in coffin; Fauchelevent will transport coffin in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery with Valjean inside; burial vault procedures complete in cemetery; Valjean emerges afterward. **FAUCHELEVENT'S CONCERN**: Initially worried earth instead of corpse won't seem real, will get displaced, will move about; men will bear it and government will notice. **SOLUTION**: Valjean's composure and prior escape experience prevailed over Fauchelevent's hesitation and over-prudence. Fauchelevent compared to cat pausing between two half-shut door leaves, prone to halt in indecision; but Valjean's coolness overcame hesitation. **CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; speaks freely; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass of good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude toward end of days. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; renders good action absolutely necessary; enlisted self-devotion, good will, old rustic cunning. **RELATIONSHIP WITH FATHER MESTIENNE**: Within last two years, made good Father Mestienne (grave-digger at Vaugirard cemetery, chubby-cheeked person), drunk at least ten times; plays with him, makes him dance according to whim; Mestienne's head adjusted to Fauchelevent's will. Fauchelevent's confidence perfect. **CURRENT EMOTIONAL STATE**: Twin plots—one with nuns, one against convent through government, one with M. Madeleine—succeeded to all appearance; limped along behind hearse in very contented frame of mind; no longer felt doubtful as to success. **STATUS**: Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence.

## Javert's Pursuit and Ongoing Investigation
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS** (January 1823): When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail, Javert attached to Paris police force. **NEWSPAPER REPORT** (December 1823): Newspaper announced Valjean's death; Javert remarked "That's a good entry." **REACTIVATION**: Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived Javert's memory; suspected Valjean had sought daughter. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead was magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern, led astray. **STRATEGIC PURSUIT**: Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily (considered it risky, preferred gloating anticipation). **CURRENT STATUS** (Winter Year 2): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. Free press embarrasses police; arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers; police agents afraid of mistakes.

## Narrative Commentary
Author remarks that burial of Mother Crucifixion under altar of convent is perfectly venial offence—one of faults which resemble duty. Nuns committed it without difficulty, even with applause of own consciences. In cloister, "government" is only intermeddling with authority, always questionable. Rule takes precedence over code. Tribute to Cæsar never anything but remnants of tribute to God. Prince is nothing in presence of principle.

## Unidentified Characters in Harbor Towns Passages
Luvie, Wilwick (eldest son of Vesmira Thornmere received sealed letter from Luvie), Gadrek Prydenridge, Isric, Jotho (discussing oats prices with carter), Tatho Brackick, wife of Tatho Brackick, Yewyn Haskick (complained of aching back), Pelde (laughed at story), Yera Stenworth—all appear in English harbor town settings with recurring motifs of weather, commerce, mundane activities. Function and narrative purpose unclear; may represent parallel storylines or thematic counterpoint.
